title: Enforce chat tool usage parity
description:
Problem: MemorySmith currently has multiple tool-availability surfaces: runtime tool descriptors in `ChatToolCatalog.cs`, MCP exposure in `McpController.cs`, documented public MCP tables in `README.md`, and chat/agent guidance in `wiki-chat-agent.md`. The differences are partly intentional, but there is no strong parity contract ensuring chat tool usage documentation and runtime capability messages stay perfectly aligned.

Desired outcome: define and test a perfect parity contract so Chat mode, Agent mode, MCP mode, and coding-agent integrations all agree on which tools are available, which are forbidden, and which policy gates explain the difference.

Scope:
- In scope: document explicit parity rules and intentional exceptions across README, prompt docs, and runtime descriptors.
- In scope: add focused tests or validation scripts that detect drift in chat tool usage contracts.
- In scope: ensure chat tool usage remains perfectly aligned with the actual intercepted tool subset and capability gating.
- Out of scope: removing all mode distinctions; the goal is verified parity, not forced identical tool sets everywhere.

Validation:
- Focused parity checks or tests fail when prompt/docs/runtime drift and pass when they align.
- Updated docs clearly describe the allowed tool set for each mode and any intentional exception.

Confidence target: 92%.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from self-review to make chat tool usage parity a first-class contract across runtime descriptors, prompt docs, MCP docs, and coding-agent expectations.
